Q: Layered Structure of Computer Networking A:

The layered architecture approach of TCP/IP protocol stack is for Distribution of work at respective layers. If you have fewer layers, you will also have to modify other adjacent layers so that the task performed by absent layers are performed by someone else.

Making a two layer only system would need a very complex layer (in your case "Everything Else" layer). which is not practical.

Q: Why web applications split into client/backend architecture, where traditional software could contain both A:

It's only a browser. It can be pretty powerful with the appropriate client-side scripting, but it's still intended to be a pretty thin client compared to a full-0blown application installed on each desktop.
